answers.answer: The initial draw deck is the 12 Speed cards, 3 Starting Upgrade cards, and 3 Stress cards shuffled together. Put 6 Heat cards face up on the Engine spot, set the Gear pawn to 1st, and draw 7 cards.
answers.evidence: Setup: 'Shuffle your 12 Speed cards, 3 Starting Upgrade cards, and 3 Stress cards together as your draw deck'; 'Place 6 Heat cards face up on the Engine spot'; 'Set Gear pawn to 1st gear'; 'Draw 7 cards'.

answers.answer: Yes, you may stay in your current gear. You may shift two positions from 1st to 3rd by paying 1 Heat immediately during Shift Gears, moving it from Engine to discard. You must have that Heat available then; Heat in hand cannot pay.
answers.evidence: Shift Gears: 'Stay in your current gear, or shift up or down one position for free'; shift two positions by 'immediately paying 1 Heat during this step: move a Heat card from your Engine to your discard pile.' Paying Heat says Heat in hand cannot pay.

answers.answer: No. In 3rd gear you must play 3 cards from hand, face down; playing only two is not allowed when you have enough playable cards.
answers.evidence: Play Cards: 'Play cards from hand face down equal to your gear number' (3rd gear = 3).

answers.answer: Steps 1 and 2 (Shift Gears and Play Cards) are simultaneous for all players. Wait until everyone completes both before step 3. Then each player completes steps 3–9 before the next player starts, proceeding frontmost to last. If side by side, the car closest to the Race Line is ahead and acts first.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure and Sequential Phase: all players complete steps 1 and 2 simultaneously; 'Each player completes all of steps 3–9 before the next player begins'; side-by-side Race Line rule.

answers.answer: Cars do not block passage through spaces. If the destination space is full, put your car in the first free spot behind the blocking cars. When placing, use the spot closest to the Race Line if it is available.
answers.evidence: Blocked Movement: 'Cars never block passage'; if destination is full, 'place your car in the first free spot behind the blocking cars.' Reveal & Move says place on spot closest to Race Line if available.

answers.answer: Each flipped non-Speed card (the Heat and Starting Upgrade) is immediately discarded. The revealed Speed 3 goes into the Play Area on top of the played Stress card and supplies that Stress card's speed. The played Stress remains underneath and both are discarded during Replenish Hand. Resolve all played Stress cards before Adrenaline.
answers.evidence: Stress Cards: discard each flipped non-Speed card, including Heat and Starting Upgrade; put found Speed card in Play Area on top of played Stress; its value supplies speed; resolve all played Stress before Adrenaline.

answers.answer: In a five-car race, the last two cars to move receive Adrenaline. Each gets access to 1 extra Cooldown and may add 1 extra speed. The extra speed may be taken before or after Boost. Unused Adrenaline cannot be saved for another round.
answers.evidence: Adrenaline: 'If the race started with 5 or more cars, the last two cars to move receive these benefits'; benefits are 1 extra Cooldown and 1 extra speed; speed before or after Boost; unused Adrenaline cannot be saved.

answers.answer: Yes. During React, you may use your 2nd-gear Cooldown allowance of 1 to move the Heat card from your hand into your Engine, then immediately spend it to Boost. Cooldown and Boost can be activated in any order, and the summary explicitly allows cooling Heat and immediately spending it. You need the Heat in the Engine when paying the Boost cost.
answers.evidence: Actions—Cooldown: 2nd gear provides Cooldown 1. React: activate Cooldown and/or Boost in any order; 'You may Cooldown Heat from your hand into your Engine, then immediately spend it to Boost.'

answers.answer: You may Boost once per turn during React. It costs 1 Heat from Engine to discard; with no Heat available in Engine you cannot Boost unless you first use available Cooldown during React to return Heat to Engine. Flip and discard non-Speed cards until a Speed card appears; add it to your Play Area and move its value. Boost speed counts for corner checks.
answers.evidence: Boost: 'Once per turn during React, pay 1 Heat from Engine to discard'; flip until a Speed card, add and move its value; 'Boost increases your total speed for corner checks.' Paying Heat covers no-Heat constraint and Cooldown option.

answers.answer: Slipstream is optional. For the corner crossed while Slipstreaming, check your round speed of 6, excluding the two Slipstream spaces. Since 6 exceeds the limit 4 by 2, pay 2 Heat.
answers.evidence: Slipstream: 'optionally move 2 spaces'; movement does not increase speed for corner checks but crossing a Corner Line still requires checking. Check Corner: pay Heat equal to speed in excess of limit.

answers.answer: Check both corners, in the order crossed. At speed 8, pay 2 Heat for the limit-6 corner and 4 for the limit-4 corner, 6 Heat total.
answers.evidence: Check Corner: 'Check every Corner Line crossed this turn ... in the order crossed'; for each separately compare total speed and pay excess.

answers.answer: The limit-4 corner at speed 7 requires 3 Heat, but you have only 2, so you spin out. Move all remaining Engine Heat to your discard pile, then move back to the first available space before the corner that caused the spin out. Take 2 extra Stress cards directly into your hand (4th gear), then set your Gear pawn to 1st.
answers.evidence: Spin Out: if unable to pay enough, move all remaining Engine Heat to discard; move to first available space before the corner; take 1 Stress in 1st/2nd or 2 in 3rd/4th directly into hand; move Gear pawn to 1st.

answers.answer: You may discard unwanted Speed cards, but not Stress or Heat cards. You may not browse any discard pile, including your own; only the top card of each pile is public knowledge.
answers.evidence: Discard step: optionally discard unwanted cards, 'but never Stress or Heat'; nobody may browse any discard pile; only top card of each pile is public knowledge.

answers.answer: Move all Play Area cards to your discard pile, then draw only enough to bring your hand back to 7; do not draw seven additional cards.
answers.evidence: Replenish Hand: 'Move all Play Area cards to your discard pile, then draw only enough cards to bring your hand back to 7. Do not draw seven additional cards.'

answers.answer: Shuffle your discard pile into a new draw deck, then continue the interrupted Stress flips. Do not include cards still in your Play Area; they have not yet been discarded.
answers.evidence: Running Out of Cards: when draw deck is empty, shuffle discard pile into a new draw deck and continue interrupted draws or flips; do not include cards still in Play Area.

answers.answer: Paying Heat moves it from Engine to discard. It can cycle from discard to draw deck to hand, and only Cooldown returns it to Engine. Heat cards cannot normally be played or voluntarily discarded from hand.
answers.evidence: Paying Heat: Engine to discard; Heat Card Cycle: 'Engine to discard to draw deck to hand; only returns to Engine via Cooldown'; Heat cards cannot normally be played or voluntarily discarded from hand.

answers.answer: Commit your two playable cards and fill the other two required slots with Heat cards in the Play Area. Your car moves zero spaces. Set your gear to 1st, discard all committed cards including the covering Heat, and skip directly to step 9. You skip React, so cannot Cooldown or Boost this turn.
answers.evidence: Cluttered Hand: commit all playable cards and fill remaining slots with Heat; car moves zero; set gear to 1st; discard all committed cards; skip directly to step 9; cannot Cooldown or Boost.

answers.answer: No, crossing first in the round does not automatically decide it. If multiple cars finish in the same round, the car furthest ahead wins; closest to Race Line breaks a tie. At the end of the round, remove all cars that crossed the final finish line and place them in finishing order on the Hall of Fame.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: same-round finishers, furthest ahead wins and Race Line breaks ties; end of round remove all final finishers and place them in finishing order on Hall of Fame.

answers.answer: No. On the final lap you cannot Slipstream across the finish line, and you cannot Slipstream after crossing it. After crossing the final finish line, ignore speed limits of corners beyond it and move as far as you can.
answers.evidence: Final-lap rules: cannot Slipstream across or after crossing the final finish line; after crossing, ignore speed limits of corners beyond it.

answers.answer: Both remaining cars receive Adrenaline if they are the last two to move. Eligibility is based on the six cars that started the race, even after finishers leave, so the last two qualify in a race that started with at least five cars.
answers.evidence: Adrenaline: eligibility uses number of cars that started, even after finishers leave; 5 or more starters means last two cars to move receive benefits.

answers.answer: Use the number of laps printed on the selected board. The summary says the USA track normally uses 2 laps and suggests a 1-lap learning race for a first USA game.
answers.evidence: Setup: 'Use the number of laps printed on the selected board'; for first USA learning race, 'just 1 lap instead of its normal 2.'

answers.answer: Do not assume every track uses exactly 6 Heat and 3 Stress. Check the board for how many Heat and Stress cards each player adds; the summary says it is typically 6 Heat and 3 Stress.
answers.evidence: Setup: 'Check the board for how many Heat and Stress cards each player adds (typically 6 Heat and 3 Stress).'

answers.answer: Randomly assign participating cars to the starting grid, placing them one at a time and filling numbered spots in ascending order. This sets first-round order. Players do not choose preferred starting positions.
answers.evidence: Setup: randomly assign cars, place one at a time in ascending numbered spots; this determines first-round order; players do not choose preferred positions.

answers.answer: Place the remaining Stress cards face up near the board as a reserve.
answers.evidence: Setup: 'Place the remaining Stress cards face up near the board as a reserve.'

answers.answer: The optional handicap is for the experienced driver to remove 1 or 2 Heat from their own car.
answers.evidence: Optional handicap: 'An experienced driver racing beginners may remove 1 or 2 Heat from their own car.'

answers.answer: No. The largest permitted shift is two gear positions, and it costs 1 Heat; shifting from 1st to 4th is three positions and is not permitted in one step.
answers.evidence: Shift Gears allows a free shift of one position or a paid shift of two positions; Player Reference: Shift 2 gears costs 1 Heat.

answers.answer: No. The two-position shift costs Heat immediately during Shift Gears, from Engine to discard, and you must have that Heat available during that step. Heat in hand cannot pay, and later Cooldown cannot retroactively pay for the shift.
answers.evidence: Shift Gears: pay 1 Heat 'immediately ... during this step' from Engine to discard and must have it available; Paying Heat says Heat in hand cannot pay.

answers.answer: Yes, resolve each Stress card by flipping until a Speed card appears; each has its own found Speed card. The total is 2 + 3 + 4 = 9 speed. The found Speed cards are added to the Play Area to supply the Stress cards' speed; they are not additional cards committed from hand.
answers.evidence: Stress Cards says 'For each Stress card you played, flip cards ... until a Speed card appears' and the found card supplies that Stress card's speed. Summary does not explicitly say they do not count as hand commitments; that follows from its description of revealed cards being added to Play Area, rather than played from hand.

answers.answer: No. You cannot voluntarily stop short to avoid a corner; move forward exactly the total speed unless blocked movement forces shorter movement.
answers.evidence: Reveal & Move: 'You cannot voluntarily stop short to avoid a corner'; a full destination can force shorter movement under Blocked Movement.

answers.answer: Use speed 8, not the five spaces moved, for the corner check. The limit-6 corner costs 2 Heat if you can pay.
answers.evidence: Check Corner: compare total speed for the round with limit; use the same total speed for each corner. Blocked movement shortens movement but not the stated round speed.

answers.answer: No. You check corners whose Corner Line you cross; being near a corner without crossing its line does not trigger a check or Heat payment.
answers.evidence: Check Corner: check every Corner Line crossed this turn; Player Reference says Check Corner only if crossed Corner Line.

answers.answer: At speed 6 or below the limit, you pay nothing and do not spin out merely because the Engine is empty. Heat is due only for speed in excess of the corner limit.
answers.evidence: Check Corner: 'If your speed does not exceed a corner's limit, pay nothing for that corner'; Spin Out applies if you cannot pay required Heat.

answers.answer: You can pay the full 3 Heat and continue. The summary says you spin out only if you cannot pay enough; it does not require retaining Heat after paying the cost.
answers.evidence: Spin Out: 'If you cannot pay enough Heat for a corner' you spin out; Paying Heat moves the required Heat from Engine to discard.

answers.answer: Pay 2 Heat at the limit-6 corner, leaving 3. The limit-4 corner then requires 4, so that is where you spin out. Move the remaining Engine Heat to discard and return to the first available space before that second corner. Take 2 Stress cards directly into hand (4th gear) and set gear to 1st.
answers.evidence: Check Corner: excess per corner, in order (8−6=2; 8−4=4). Spin Out rules specify all remaining Heat to discard, return before the causing corner, 2 Stress in 3rd/4th directly into hand, gear to 1st.

answers.answer: Take 1 extra Stress card directly into your hand and move your Gear pawn to 1st gear.
answers.evidence: Spin Out: 1 extra Stress in 1st/2nd gear, directly into hand; then move Gear pawn to 1st.

answers.answer: 1st gear provides Cooldown 3. With Adrenaline's extra 1 Cooldown, you can cool up to 4 Heat cards from hand to Engine. Cooling is optional; the summary says you may Cooldown, not that you must use all available cooling.
answers.evidence: Player Reference: 1st gear Cooldown 3. Adrenaline: 1 extra Cooldown. Actions—Cooldown permits moving Heat from hand back to Engine, but the summary does not explicitly state that using available Cooldown is optional or that all cooling may be declined.

answers.answer: Yes. Adrenaline's extra Cooldown and extra speed are separate benefits; you may use the extra Cooldown without adding the extra speed. The summary does not expressly state that the extra speed can be declined, so that part is unsupported.
answers.evidence: Adrenaline grants access to '1 extra Cooldown and may add 1 extra speed.' The summary does not explicitly discuss declining either benefit.

answers.answer: Yes. Adrenaline eligibility is based on the order cars moved, so the last car to move remains eligible even if it ends in the lead. In a four-car race, only the last car to move receives it; the second-to-last does not, because the last two rule applies only when at least five cars started.
answers.evidence: Adrenaline: last car to move gains benefits; if race started with 5 or more cars, last two do; use the number that started the race.

answers.answer: You qualify if you end next to another car or in the space immediately behind a car. If neither, you do not qualify.
answers.evidence: Slipstream: 'If you end next to another car or in the space immediately behind a car, optionally move 2 spaces forward.'

answers.answer: Yes. Eligibility is checked at the Slipstream step based on where you end after Reveal & Move and React, so a Boost that lands you immediately behind a car can make you eligible. The summary does not explicitly discuss this timing example, but its step sequence supports it.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure orders React before Slipstream; Slipstream condition says 'If you end next to another car or in the space immediately behind a car.' Boost takes place during React and moves the car.

answers.answer: Just one optional two-space Slipstream move; the summary describes a single move if you end next to another car or immediately behind a car, without stacking per qualifying car.
answers.evidence: Slipstream describes one optional move of 2 spaces when you meet the adjacency condition; it does not explicitly address qualifying relative to multiple cars.

answers.answer: Slipstream does not allow sharing an occupied spot. If its full landing space is occupied, use the normal Blocked Movement placement rule, placing in the first free spot behind the blocking cars. The reduced movement does not change corner-check speed; Slipstream movement is excluded from corner-check speed.
answers.evidence: Slipstream: full landing space uses normal Blocked Movement placement; does not permit sharing; shorter movement does not change corner-check speed.

answers.answer: The final finish line does not waive the corner before it: pay 4 Heat for the limit-4 corner at speed 8. Ignore the limit-3 corner beyond the final finish line, so total Heat due is 4.
answers.evidence: Scoring: after crossing final finish line, ignore speed limits of corners beyond it. Check Corner requires paying speed excess at corners crossed; 8−4=4.

answers.answer: Yes, an otherwise legal Slipstream may cross the start/finish line on an intermediate lap, and corners beyond it still have their normal speed limits.
answers.evidence: Scoring: on intermediate laps an otherwise legal Slipstream may cross start/finish; normal corner speed limits still apply beyond it.

answers.answer: The remaining cars keep racing. At the end of the round, remove cars that crossed the final finish line and place them on the Hall of Fame; continue playing until all cars finish.
answers.evidence: Scoring: 'At the end of the round, remove all cars that crossed the final finish line ... Continue playing until all cars finish.'

answers.answer: No. In the core game, only crossing a Corner Line triggers a corner check. The Legends Line is used only in advanced play; crossing it alone is not a core-game payment trigger.
answers.evidence: Track Lines: 'In the core game, a Corner Line triggers a corner check'; Legends Line is used only in advanced play and crossing it alone is not a core-game trigger.

answers.answer: No. Gear shifting happens before card commitment, and you play cards equal to your gear number. After shifting from 3rd to 2nd, you commit 2 cards; with two playable cards, you have enough and do not trigger Cluttered Hand merely because you began in 3rd.
answers.evidence: Simultaneous Phase: Shift Gears is step 1 and Play Cards is step 2; Play Cards count is based on gear number. Cluttered Hand applies when Heat leaves too few playable cards for your gear.
